document_title: 813 gas generators for one AI data center, and who pays
_note: Slide strings set from the storyboard dossiers; each carries its claim ids.
caption:
Up to five years in El Paso Electric's plan. The life of the plant in the judges'.

The plant would be 813 gas generators beside Meta's AI data center in northeast El Paso County. The data center would carry the plant's capital costs for a bridge of up to five years. After that the utility wanted flexibility on who pays. Any change would need Commission approval in a separate case.

Two judges recommend approval only if other customers are held harmless from the plant's capital and operating costs for its life. Otherwise they would recommend denial. The condition lifts only if the utility shows the plant meets the statute's test.

El Paso City Council has authorized a counteroffer for a full hold harmless.

The judges' findings put the plant's total estimated cost at approximately $499.8 million. How much of that has a named payer after the bridge?

S1.headline: 813 gas generators. One customer.
S1.cite: c1 c2 c3 c6 c8 c9 c28 c38 c39 DRAWN
S1.body: El Paso Electric wants to build them beside Meta's AI data center in northeast El Paso County, at first the plant's only retail customer. Two judges have now filed a proposal for decision with a condition on who pays.
strings: El Paso Electric wants to build them beside Meta's AI data center in northeast El Paso County, at first the plant's only retail customer. Two judges have now filed a proposal for decision with a condition on who pays.

S2.headline: Four or five to a transformer
S2.body: The plan would buy 813 modular gas generators rated at 450 kilowatts each. They are typically installed in groups of four or five, each group connected to a step-up transformer.
strings: Four or five to a transformer
The plan would buy 813 modular gas generators rated at 450 kilowatts each. They are typically installed in groups of four or five, each group connected to a step-up transformer.

S3.headline: About 31 acres beside the data center
S3.cite: c1 c2 c3 c6 c8 c9 DRAWN
S3.body: The plant would sit immediately next to Meta's newest AI data center, which Wurldwide LLC is developing. That data center is intended at first to be the only retail customer of the plant's output.

S4.headline: 366 MW against 1,000
S4.cite: c1 c10 c11 c12 c13 DRAWN
S4.body: The data center has committed to 1,000 MW by the end of 2029. The judges found existing resources can serve about the first 220 MW of its load, and the second 220 MW requires additional capacity.
strings: The data center has committed to 1,000 MW by the end of 2029. The judges found existing resources can serve about the first 220 MW of its load, and the second 220 MW requires additional capacity.

S5.headline: Need shown. The rest, not.
S5.body: The two judges filed their proposal for decision on September 23rd. They found the utility showed a need for capacity to serve the data center.
labels: did not show that the McCloud facility is a cost-effective and reliable resource
failed to show that it adequately considered alternatives

S6.headline: The vendor the data center preferred
S6.body: El Paso Electric engaged Enchanted Rock after the data center preferred it. It considered no other vendor, issued no request for proposals and ran no cost-benefit analysis for ratepayers. The plant would be its first experience with modular gas generation.

S7.headline: Up to five years, then no decision
S7.body: El Paso Electric proposes a bridge of up to five years in which the data center pays all the plant's capital costs. Its witness testified that no decision has been made on who pays after that, and any change would need Commission approval in a separate case.

S9.headline: The commission has not ruled
S9.cite: c6 c37 c42 c43 c44 c45 DRAWN
S9.body: Five commissioners will accept, change or reject the proposal at an open meeting, and KVIA reports a final order is expected by December 7th. Docket 59076 holds comments from 1118 protestors and residents.
